bull.t: Recurring subscription growth and enterprise retention
bull.b: ServiceNow’s subscription model combines recurring contract revenue with strong renewal performance and account expansion. Sustained CRPO growth and a 98% renewal rate indicate durable enterprise demand, supporting revenue visibility and continued cross-selling across the Now Platform.

bull.t: Accelerating AI monetization and platform adoption
bull.b: AI is becoming a meaningful commercial growth engine rather than only a product investment. Rising AI contract value, accelerating production deployments, and governance capabilities can deepen platform dependence and expand ServiceNow’s role in enterprise workflow automation.

bull.t: Strong cash generation and scalable profitability
bull.b: High gross margins and substantial conversion of earnings into cash demonstrate an asset-light, scalable SaaS model. Strong operating cash flow gives ServiceNow resources to fund product development, acquisitions, and sales investment while supporting financial resilience.

bear.b: The recent debt increase creates a more significant claim on future cash generation and reduces flexibility compared with the prior balance-sheet position. If elevated borrowing persists, ServiceNow may have less capacity to fund acquisitions, investment, or shareholder returns.

bear.t: Near-term subscription margin pressure from AI consumption
bear.b: AI adoption can increase infrastructure consumption before related revenue and pricing fully scale. This creates near-term pressure on subscription gross margins and makes profitability progression less predictable, even if AI monetization ultimately strengthens the longer-term growth opportunity.

Although free cash flow remains substantial, the slight TTM decline signals that cash generation is no longer accelerating at its previous pace. A sustained plateau could limit the rate at which ServiceNow funds expansion and would make operating execution more important.
